産.meaning: On a <part>stand</part> at the very edge of a <part>cliff</part>, a farmer sets out everything that springs to <part>life</part> in her garden: carrots, melons, pumpkins, plums. Hang gliders swoop past and buy as they fly. Grown right here, it's fresh <kanji>produce</kanji>.
産.on: One hang glider buys a strawberry <sound>sun</sound>dae, piled high with fruit fresh from the stand.
産.kun: '<sound>Ooh</sound>!' gasps the farmer, as her goat gives birth to twins right under the stand.

美.meaning: A sculptor carves a <part>large</part> statue of a man with a curly <part>ram's head</part>. At first the whole village laughs at it. But at sunrise the gold horns catch the light, and the crowd falls silent. It's pure <kanji>beauty</kanji>.
美.on: A shiny green <sound>bee</sound>tle lands on one horn and sparkles like a jewel.
美.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' gasps the crowd, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the sculptor in the stone dust, and a <sound>coo</sound>k drops his pan to stare.

術.meaning: At a busy <part>crossroads</part>, a juggler plucks the single apple off a scrawny <part>apple tree</part>, tosses it up with two knives and catches it peeled, cored and sliced. Cars stop to honk and clap. Years of practice went into that: it's <kanji>art</kanji>.
術.on: A <sound>ju</sound>ry of pigeons gives him top marks, and one sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' on the apple peel.
術.kun: His only means of making a living: juggling <sound>su</sound>shi on the corner, then sleeping in a <sound>be</sound>d of apple peel.

箱.meaning: Two beavers on opposite banks gnaw <part>bamboo</part> canes and weave them into walls, each one copying the other across the river in <part>mutual</part> silence. They meet in the middle, slot their two halves together and tie a lid on top. It's a <kanji>box</kanji>.
箱.on: They pack a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p inside, because beavers like to keep clean.
箱.kun: They post the box to a <sound>hu</sound>t in the woods, where a <sound>ko</sound>ala opens it and washes its paws.

痢.meaning: The castaway who turned a <part>profit</part> on bread rolls eats the last stale one himself. All night long he dashes back and forth to the <part>leaky shed</part> behind his camp, drips plopping on his head, tummy gurgling. He's got <kanji>diarrhea</kanji>.
痢.on: He spends the next day lying weak on the warm <sound>ree</sound>f, swearing never to eat bread again.

算.meaning: A shopkeeper builds an abacus from thin <part>bamboo</part> rods and props it up on a little <part>goal</part> frame. With one sharp <part>eye</part> on the beads, she clicks them back and forth, adding up the whole day's takings in seconds. She can <kanji>calculate</kanji> anything.
算.on: Then she works out exactly how many cherries go on each ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae.
算.kun: She does her sums lying on a <sound>so</sound>fa, while a <sound>ro</sound>dent slides the beads for her.

精.meaning: In a jeweller's window, on <part>blue</part> velvet, lie a hundred grains of <part>rice</part>, polished one by one until they shine like tiny pearls. The price tag has a lot of zeros. Nothing in the shop is more <kanji>refined</kanji>.
精.on: At night the jeweller locks the rice away in a heavy steel <sound>sa</sound>fe.
精.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p rubs each grain with its wool, and the jeweller cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!': polished to a shine.

趣.meaning: A <part>runner</part> races through a library that closes in five minutes. From each book she has time to <part>take</part> just one line as she flies past the shelves. At the door, panting, she can tell you what every book was about: its <kanji>purport</kanji>.
趣.on: She keeps going on a <sound>su</sound>gar cube tucked in her cheek.
趣.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' she gasps at the last book, where a <sound>mo</sound>le and a <sound>moo</sound>se share the <sound>key</sound> to a secret garden. What charm.

誕.meaning: The mayor's <part>speech</part> drags on and on, and each time he nearly stops, he finds a way to <part>prolong</part> it. Halfway through, a woman in the front row gasps, and a baby is born right there in the hall. Nobody remembers the speech: everyone talks about the <kanji>nativity</kanji>.
誕.on: The baby is rushed home through a long dark <sound>tun</sound>nel, crying the whole way.
